source: 2019 Alabama Course of Study: Mathematics, Mathematical Modeling (MM.1-MM.22), standard text verified against the official ALSDE PDF (alabama-cos-mathematics-2019.pdf). Domains/clusters are the standard Alabama groupings. No DIGS critical flags exist for these courses in Eddie's files, so critical is false for all — do not treat that as a DIGS marking.

standards.cluster: Mathematical modeling and statistical problem-solving are extensive, cyclical processes that can be used to answer significant real-world problems.
standards.text: Use the full Mathematical Modeling Cycle or Statistical Problem-Solving Cycle to answer a real-world problem of particular student interest, incorporating standards from across the course.

standards.cluster: Mathematical models involving growth and decay are useful in solving real-world problems involving borrowing and investing; spreadsheets are a frequently-used and powerful tool to assist with modeling financial situations.
standards.text: Use elements of the Mathematical Modeling Cycle to solve real-world problems involving finances.

standards.cluster: Mathematical models involving growth and decay are useful in solving real-world problems involving borrowing and investing; spreadsheets are a frequently-used and powerful tool to assist with modeling financial situations.
standards.text: Organize and display financial information using geometric sequences to represent compound interest and proportional depreciation, including periodic (yearly, monthly, weekly) and continuous compounding.

parts.text: Explain the relationship between annual percentage yield (APY) and annual percentage rate (APR) as values for r in the formulas A=P(1+r)t and A=Pert.

standards.cluster: Mathematical models involving growth and decay are useful in solving real-world problems involving borrowing and investing; spreadsheets are a frequently-used and powerful tool to assist with modeling financial situations.
standards.text: Compare simple and compound interest, and straight-line and proportional depreciation.

standards.cluster: Mathematical models involving growth and decay are useful in solving real-world problems involving borrowing and investing; spreadsheets are a frequently-used and powerful tool to assist with modeling financial situations.
standards.text: Investigate growth and reduction of credit card debt using spreadsheets, including variables such as beginning balance, payment structures, credits, interest rates, new purchases, finance charges, and fees.

standards.cluster: Mathematical models involving growth and decay are useful in solving real-world problems involving borrowing and investing; spreadsheets are a frequently-used and powerful tool to assist with modeling financial situations.
standards.text: Compare and contrast housing finance options including renting, leasing to purchase, purchasing with a mortgage, and purchasing with cash.

parts.text: Research and evaluate various mortgage products available to consumers.
Compare monthly mortgage payments for different terms, interest rates, and down payments.

Analyze the financial consequence of buying a home (mortgage payments vs. potentially increasing resale value) versus investing the money saved when renting, assuming that renting is the less expensive option.

standards.text: Investigate the advantages and disadvantages of various means of paying for an automobile, including leasing, purchasing by cash, and purchasing by loan.

standards.cluster: Two- and three-dimensional representations, coordinates systems, geometric transformations, and scale models are useful tools in planning, designing, and constructing solutions to real-world problems.
standards.text: Use the Mathematical Modeling Cycle to solve real-world problems involving the design of three-dimensional objects.

standards.cluster: Two- and three-dimensional representations, coordinates systems, geometric transformations, and scale models are useful tools in planning, designing, and constructing solutions to real-world problems.
standards.text: Construct a two-dimensional visual representation of a three-dimensional object or structure.

parts.text: Determine the level of precision and the appropriate tools for taking the measurements in constructing a two-dimensional visual representation of a three-dimensional object or structure.
Create an elevation drawing to represent a given solid structure, using technology where appropriate.

Determine which measurements cannot be taken directly and must be calculated based on other measurements when constructing a two-dimensional visual representation of a three-dimensional object or structure.
Determine an appropriate means to visually represent an object or structure, such as drawings on paper or graphics on computer screens.

standards.cluster: Two- and three-dimensional representations, coordinates systems, geometric transformations, and scale models are useful tools in planning, designing, and constructing solutions to real-world problems.
standards.text: Plot coordinates on a three-dimensional Cartesian coordinate system and use relationships between coordinates to solve design problems.

parts.text: Describe the features of a three-dimensional Cartesian coordinate system and use them to graph points.
Graph a point in space as the vertex of a right prism drawn in the appropriate octant with edges along the x, y, and z axes.
Find the distance between two objects in space given the coordinates of each.
Find the midpoint between two objects in space given the coordinates of each.

standards.cluster: Two- and three-dimensional representations, coordinates systems, geometric transformations, and scale models are useful tools in planning, designing, and constructing solutions to real-world problems.
standards.text: Use technology and other tools to explore the results of simple transformations using three-dimensional coordinates, including translations in the x, y, and/or z directions; rotations of 90º, 180º, or 270º about the x, y, and z axes; reflections over the xy, yz, and xy planes; and dilations from the origin.

standards.cluster: Two- and three-dimensional representations, coordinates systems, geometric transformations, and scale models are useful tools in planning, designing, and constructing solutions to real-world problems.
standards.text: Create a scale model of a complex three-dimensional structure based on observed measurements and indirect measurements, using translations, reflections, rotations, and dilations of its components.

standards.domain: Creating Functions to Model Change in the Environment and Society
standards.cluster: Functions can be used to represent general trends in conditions that change over time and to predict future conditions based on present observations.
standards.text: Use elements of the Mathematical Modeling Cycle to make predictions based on measurements that change over time, including motion, growth, decay, and cycling.

standards.cluster: Functions can be used to represent general trends in conditions that change over time and to predict future conditions based on present observations.
standards.text: Use regression with statistical graphing technology to determine an equation that best fits a set of bivariate data, including nonlinear patterns.

parts.text: Create a scatter plot with a sufficient number of data points to predict a pattern.
Describe the overall relationship between two quantitative variables (increase, decrease, linearity, concavity, extrema, inflection) or pattern of change.
Make a prediction based upon patterns.

standards.text: Create a linear representation of non-linear data and interpret solutions, using technology and the process of linearization with logarithms.

standards.cluster: Statistical studies allow a conclusion to be drawn about a population that is too large to survey completely or about cause and effect in an experiment.
standards.text: Use the Statistical Problem Solving Cycle to answer real-world questions.

standards.cluster: Statistical studies allow a conclusion to be drawn about a population that is too large to survey completely or about cause and effect in an experiment.
standards.text: Construct a probability distribution based on empirical observations of a variable.

parts.text: Estimate the probability of each value for a random variable based on empirical observations or simulations, using technology.
Represent a probability distribution by a relative frequency histogram and/or a cumulative relative frequency graph.

Find the mean, standard deviation, median, and interquartile range of a probability distribution and make long-term predictions about future possibilities. Determine which measures are most appropriate based upon the shape of the distribution.

standards.cluster: Statistical studies allow a conclusion to be drawn about a population that is too large to survey completely or about cause and effect in an experiment.
standards.text: Construct a sampling distribution for a random event or random sample.

parts.text: Use the binomial theorem to construct the sampling distribution for the number of successes in a binary event or the number of positive responses to a yes/no question in a random sample.
Use the normal approximation of a proportion from a random event or sample when conditions are met.
Use the central limit theorem to construct a normal sampling distribution for the sample mean when conditions are met.
Find the long-term probability of a given range of outcomes from a random event or random sample.

standards.cluster: Statistical studies allow a conclusion to be drawn about a population that is too large to survey completely or about cause and effect in an experiment.
standards.text: Perform inference procedures based on the results of samples and experiments.

parts.text: Use a point estimator and margin of error to construct a confidence interval for a proportion or mean.
Interpret a confidence interval in context and use it to make strategic decisions.
Perform a significance test for null and alternative hypotheses.
Interpret the significance level of a test in the context of error probabilities, and use the results to make strategic decisions.

standards.cluster: Statistical studies allow a conclusion to be drawn about a population that is too large to survey completely or about cause and effect in an experiment.
standards.text: Critique the validity of reported conclusions from statistical studies in terms of bias and random error probabilities.

standards.cluster: Statistical studies allow a conclusion to be drawn about a population that is too large to survey completely or about cause and effect in an experiment.
standards.text: Conduct a randomized study on a topic of student interest (sample or experiment) and draw conclusions based upon the results.
